userStories.title: Move non-blocking-fix configuration to review with reviewer sources
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move the non-blocking-fix config slice to `review.nonBlockingFix`, add its per-reviewer source selection, and preserve legacy configuration through a warning migration.

**Motivation** — Both reviewers build the same `advisoryFindings` bucket, deliberately so since #1865 / PR #1908; `semantic-review.ts:440-445` says as much in a comment. But the nbf seed reads one phase by name (`execution-plan.ts:397`), so the semantic bucket is reported at run end and then dropped.

**Approach** — **Per-reviewer seeding is a config `sources` list, not a widened boolean.** The four states operators need are adversarial-only, semantic-only, both, and neither. A `sources` array expresses all four in one place and keeps a single set of `scope` / `sourceDiffCap` knobs governing the one fix pass.

**The nbf block moves to `review.nonBlockingFix`.** It currently lives inside `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema` (`schemas-review.ts:167`), which is why the seed was adversarial-shaped in the first place. Configuring semantic's opt-in under `review.adversarial` would reproduce that drift. The legacy path keeps working through a migration shim, per the project's config conventions: a benign rename with no semantic change takes a shim that warns, copies to the new key and drops the old — not a pre-parse reject guard, which is reserved for removals that would silently drop behaviour.

**`sources` defaults to `["adversarial"]`.** Existing configs behave exactly as today and semantic seeding is opt-in, matching how nbf itself shipped ("Opt-in; ramp to true after validating signal quality").

The default is declared with Zod's `.default()`, per the project's config convention that defaults live in the schema. The consequence is deliberate and must not be "simplified" away: `.default()` makes `sources` **required on the inferred output type**, so every existing object literal passed where a `NonBlockingFixConfig` is expected stops typechecking until it names the field. US-001's `Modifies` list authorises exactly those files. Declaring `sources` as `.optional()` and resolving the fallback at the read site would avoid the cascade but would move a default out of the schema, which the convention forbids.

**Scope** — In: standalone exported nbf schema; `ReviewConfigSchema.nonBlockingFix`; the inferred type alias; legacy-to-canonical compat migration and per-layer precedence; affected typed nbf literals and canonical config fixtures. Out: consuming `sources` to seed reviewer findings (US-002); changing nbf's `scope`, `sourceDiffCap`, `regressionAttempts` or `verifierGuard` semantics, or making any of them per-source. One fix pass, one set of knobs.

**Interface** — `sources: z.array(z.enum(["adversarial", "semantic"])).default(["adversarial"])`. The target alias is derived from the new standalone nbf schema, so the type carries `sources` and no longer depends on `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema`. A new exported migration moves `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` to `review.nonBlockingFix`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `review.nonBlockingFix` is parsed as an empty object, then its resolved slice has `enabled: false`, `scope: "both"`, `regressionAttempts: 1`, `verifierGuard: true`, and `sourceDiffCap: { maxFiles: 10, maxLines: 500 }`.
When `review.nonBlockingFix` is parsed as an empty object, then its `sources` is `["adversarial"]`.
When `review.nonBlockingFix.sources` contains `["adversarial", "semantic"]`, then parsing preserves both entries in declared order.
When `review.nonBlockingFix.sources` contains an unrecognised reviewer name, then parsing rejects with a validation error naming `sources`.
When `review.nonBlockingFix` is omitted entirely, then parsing returns `undefined` for that slice and synthesises no nbf defaults elsewhere in the parsed config.

When only legacy `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` is supplied, then parsing resolves the same nbf slice as the canonical location and emits one config warning naming both the legacy and canonical keys.
When both `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` and `review.nonBlockingFix` are supplied, then parsing resolves the canonical block's values, emits a warning naming both keys, and does not throw.
When neither legacy nor canonical nbf location is supplied, then the nbf migration returns the config unchanged and emits no config warning about nbf.

When a legacy `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` is supplied in one config layer and canonical `review.nonBlockingFix` in a later layer, then the later layer's canonical value wins after resolution, demonstrating the migration runs before layer merge.
When `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema` parses an adversarial block containing `nonBlockingFix`, then the parsed object has no `nonBlockingFix` property.

routing.reasoning: This is a conventional four-module schema and compat-shim migration with known fixture fallout, but it introduces no new runtime abstraction.

modifiedFiles.reason: every case parses through `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema` and the first asserts `cfg.nonBlockingFix` deep-equals the defaults literal. Once the block moves, that schema strips the key and the field is `undefined`, so a correct implementation fails these assertions. Replacement invariant: the same default-shape and validation assertions, made against the new standalone nbf schema and through `review.nonBlockingFix`, plus the legacy path asserted via the migration rather than via the adversarial schema.

two `as const` nbf literals are passed to `shouldRunNonBlockingFix` and `runNonBlockingFix`, both of which take a `NonBlockingFixConfig`. Once `sources` is a defaulted field it is required on that type, so the literals stop typechecking. Replacement invariant: the same retired-only gate-closure assertions, with each literal naming `sources`.

the quarantine-transaction literal is passed to `runNonBlockingFix`, whose options declare `cfg: NonBlockingFixConfig`, so it stops typechecking for the same reason. Replacement invariant: the same quarantine-transaction assertions, with the literal naming `sources`.

the literal is passed to `StoryOrchestratorBuilder.addNonBlockingFix`, whose first parameter is a `NonBlockingFixConfig`, so it stops typechecking for the same reason. Replacement invariant: the same "builder does not throw" assertion, with the literal naming `sources`.

two fixtures declare a fully-enumerated `review.adversarial` block with `nonBlockingFix` nested inside it. That key is no longer part of the adversarial schema, so the fixtures no longer describe a reachable config shape. Replacement invariant: the same triage-assembly assertions, with nbf declared at `review.nonBlockingFix` and `sources` named.

three fixtures nest `nonBlockingFix` under `review.adversarial` for the same reason. Replacement invariant: the same wiring and green-precondition assertions, with nbf declared canonically and `sources` named.

userStories.title: Seed non-blocking fixes from selected review advisory buckets
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extract non-blocking-fix seed derivation and use `sources` to union actionable semantic and adversarial advisories without changing the pass's safety gates.

**Motivation** — So the union adds 9 nbf passes (500 → 509, +2%) plus 36 findings into passes that already run.

**Approach** — Two independent changes, no shared module. The nbf work is a config move plus one extracted seam.

`src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts` — Baseline: lines ~379-410 inline the green precondition, the `advCfg` gate keyed on `this.state.adversarialReview`, the single-phase read of `phaseOutputs["adversarial-review"]`, and the `actionableAdvisoryFindings` call. Target: that derivation moves to a new module and the call site consumes its result. **This extraction is mandatory, not stylistic:** the file is exactly 600 lines, the `SRC_LIMIT` in `scripts/check-file-sizes.ts`, and it is not in `scripts/baselines/file-sizes-baseline.json` — it has zero headroom and any added line fails the ratchet.

`actionableAdvisoryFindings(findings: readonly Finding[]): readonly Finding[]` (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:65`) filters `actionRequired === false`, `acDropped === true`, and `isRecurrenceRetired(f)`. Applies unchanged to both sources.

`shouldRunNonBlockingFix(cfg: NonBlockingFixConfig | undefined, advisoryCount: number): boolean` (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:80`) requires `cfg?.enabled === true && advisoryCount > 0`.

What makes a mixed-threshold union safe today is that nbf's strategy set passes `promptSeverityFloor: "info"` at all six call sites in `build-plan-for-strategy.ts:395-427`, so the rectifier prompt's render floor never reads `review.blockingThreshold`. That is load-bearing behaviour resting on a hardcoded literal, documented only as a comment about empty findings lists and pinned by no test. US-002 pins it.

**Scope** — In: create the seed module; wire the execution-plan production path to it; repoint plan assembly to canonical nbf configuration and allow semantic-only review plans; source selection, actionability, deduplication, green gating, and render-floor tests. Out: configuration schema and migration work (US-001); static-rules logging and pressure documentation (US-003); adding a category filter to what nbf seeds. `actionableAdvisoryFindings` filters on `actionRequired`, `acDropped` and recurrence-retirement only, never on `category`, so an adversarial `out-of-scope` finding is seeded today and still will be.

**Interface** — `nbf-seed.ts` exports the seed derivation that `execution-plan.ts` calls. `actionableAdvisoryFindings(findings: readonly Finding[]): readonly Finding[]`; `shouldRunNonBlockingFix(cfg: NonBlockingFixConfig | undefined, advisoryCount: number): boolean`.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a story with two actionable semantic-review advisory findings, no adversarial-review advisories, and nbf `sources` naming both reviewers, when the seed is derived, then it returns both semantic findings.
Given the same phase outputs but nbf `sources` naming only `adversarial`, when the seed is derived, then it returns an empty list and reports that nbf should not run.
Given one actionable adversarial-review advisory and two actionable semantic-review advisories with both sources named, when the seed is derived, then it returns three findings.
Given both reviewer advisory buckets contain a finding with the same file, line, and message and both sources are named, when the seed is derived, then it returns that finding once.
Given a semantic advisory whose `meta.recurrence.disposition` is `retired` and both sources are named, when the seed is derived, then it excludes that finding.
Given a semantic advisory whose `actionRequired` is `false` and both sources are named, when the seed is derived, then it excludes that finding.
Given semantic-review did not run and both sources are named, when the seed is derived, then it returns the adversarial findings without an error.
Given any phase output fails the phase-passed predicate, when the seed is derived, then it reports that nbf should not run regardless of advisory findings.

Given rectification enabled, a story id, nbf enabled with both sources, a passing semantic-review output with one actionable advisory, and a passing adversarial-review output with none, when the story is driven through the story-orchestrator phase-completion path, then the stubbed nbf runner is invoked once with the semantic finding.
Given the prior phase-completion scenario with `sources` changed to only `adversarial`, when the story completes, then the stubbed nbf runner is not invoked.

Given `review.blockingThreshold` is `error` and then `warning`, with a warning advisory finding in each case, when the nbf strategy set builds its implementer strategy, then both strategies use severity floor `info` and render the warning finding into rectifier input.
Given a finding with `source: "semantic-review"` and `fixTarget: "source"`, when the nbf strategy set builds the autofix implementer strategy, then that strategy claims the finding.

Given review checks contain `semantic` but not `adversarial`, rectification enabled, a story id, nbf enabled with sources naming `semantic`, and a passing semantic-review output with one actionable advisory, when the story is driven through the story-orchestrator phase-completion path, then the stubbed nbf runner is invoked once with that finding.

Given the prior semantic-only review scenario with `sources` changed to only `adversarial`, when the story completes, then the stubbed nbf runner is not invoked, confirming the pass is gated by `sources` rather than by which reviewer slots the config happens to declare.

Given nbf is enabled with `sources` empty and a green story whose adversarial-review and semantic-review phases each produced one actionable advisory finding, when the seed is derived, then it returns no findings and reports that nbf should not run.

routing.reasoning: The new seed seam changes execution-plan wiring, plan assembly, reviewer-source selection, deduplication, and phase-completion integration while preserving safety gates.

userStories.title: Correct soft-mode static-rules budget warnings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make static-rules warnings accurately describe non-enforcing budget pressure while retaining existing enforced-mode output and pressure values.

**Motivation** — An operator reading the log is told rules were truncated when all of them shipped, and is pointed at a budget that is not binding.

**Approach** — Two independent changes, no shared module. The static-rules work is a log-wording change with no behavioural effect.

`src/context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts` — Baseline: the warnings at `:373` ("Canonical rules are approaching/exceeding static rules budget") and `:382` ("Rule sections truncated by static rules budget") fire off `budgetResult` with no `enforceBudget` check, both carrying `droppedCount: budgetResult.droppedIds.length`. Target: under `enforceBudget: false` the messages state that sections *would* be truncated and name the flag; under `enforceBudget: true` message text and payloads are unchanged. The file is 597 of 600 lines, so the change must be net-neutral or shrink; the provider's returned `budgetPressure` is not touched.

`src/context/engine/manifest-types.ts` — Baseline: `ProviderBudgetPressure.droppedCount` is documented as *"Items discarded to satisfy the budget. Zero unless the budget is enforced."* (`:33-34`), which is false — `static-rules.test.ts:667` pins it to 1 in soft mode. Target: the doc comment on `droppedCount` and `droppedTokens` states that under a non-enforcing budget these count sections that *would* be discarded, and that `overageTokens` is the enforcement-independent signal.

**Scope** — In: budget warning wording conditional on `enforceBudget`; unchanged enforced messages and payloads; pressure-field documentation. Out: changing what `budgetPressure.droppedCount` counts in soft mode. It remains a pressure signal — the count of sections that would be dropped — and the existing US-003 AC 3 assertion at `static-rules.test.ts:667` stays green. Only the log wording and the field documentation change.

**Interface** — `ProviderBudgetPressure.droppedCount` and `ProviderBudgetPressure.droppedTokens` document would-be discards under a non-enforcing budget; `overageTokens` remains the enforcement-independent signal.
acceptanceCriteria: Given canonical rules exceed the budget and `enforceBudget` is `false`, when `StaticRulesProvider` emits its truncation warning, then the message states that sections would be truncated, names `enforceBudget`, and does not state that sections were truncated.
Given canonical rules exceed the budget and `enforceBudget` is `true`, when `StaticRulesProvider` emits its truncation warning, then the message is unchanged from today's text.
Given canonical rules exceed the budget and `enforceBudget` is `false`, when `StaticRulesProvider` returns its result, then it contains one chunk per canonical rule with no section withheld.

Given canonical rules exceed the budget and `enforceBudget` is `false`, when `StaticRulesProvider` returns its result, then `budgetPressure.overageTokens` is non-zero and `budgetPressure.droppedCount` equals the enforcing configuration's count for the same rule set, confirming the pressure object is unchanged by this story.
Given canonical rules fit within the budget and `enforceBudget` is `false`, when `StaticRulesProvider` runs, then it emits no truncation warning.

Given the rule total reaches the approaching-budget threshold and `enforceBudget` is `false`, when `StaticRulesProvider` emits its approaching-budget warning, then the message names `enforceBudget` and does not assert that any section was dropped.

routing.reasoning: The implementation is a bounded conditional log-message and comment edit in an existing provider, with returned data explicitly unchanged.

analysis:
This feature contains two independent TypeScript changes: review/NBF configuration and orchestration, plus static-rules budget-warning truthfulness. The NBF object is currently embedded in `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema` at `src/config/schemas-review.ts:167-211`; `ReviewConfigSchema` owns `semantic` and `adversarial` at `src/config/schemas-review.ts:256-257`. `NonBlockingFixConfig` is inferred from the adversarial nesting in `src/config/selectors.ts:182`, and is used by orchestrator state (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:191`), its builder (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/builder.ts:130-138`), and non-blocking-fix helpers (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:65-90`). Moving the schema must therefore repoint the alias and update all typed object literals; a Zod `.default()` on `sources` intentionally makes the output field required.

Raw config compatibility is applied to every config layer before merge and Zod validation in `applyConfigCompatShims` (`src/config/compat-shims.ts:483-502`). The existing `migrateLegacyReviewModelKey` (`src/config/migrations.ts:100-141`) is the required model: immutable transformation, no-op identity when absent, warning-backed aliasing, and canonical-wins without throwing. The NBF shim must migrate `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` to `review.nonBlockingFix` at this per-layer point, otherwise a legacy value can incorrectly override a later canonical layer. Zod strips unknown object fields, so removing the migration would silently lose legacy behavior. Existing fixtures with legacy nesting or typed NBF literals include `test/unit/config/non-blocking-fix-config.test.ts:1-67`, `test/unit/execution/non-blocking-fix-retirement.test.ts`, `test/unit/execution/nbf-readonly-flake-triage.test.ts`, `test/unit/execution/rectification-overrides.test.ts`, `test/unit/execution/build-plan-for-strategy-triage-assembly.test.ts`, and `test/unit/execution/non-blocking-fix-wiring.test.ts`.

At execution time `buildPlanForStrategy` reads only `config.review?.adversarial?.nonBlockingFix` and only constructs NBF strategies when an adversarial input exists (`src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:369-372`); canonical configuration and semantic-only plans require this to change. The same strategy builder already uses `promptSeverityFloor: "info"` at every advisory-capable NBF strategy construction (`src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:395-427`), preserving advisory rendering regardless of the shared review threshold. The autofix implementer already claims `semantic-review` (`src/operations/autofix-implementer-strategy.ts:11`).

`ExecutionPlan` currently computes the green precondition, gates on an adversarial state slot, reads just `phaseOutputs["adversarial-review"]`, and filters advisories inline at `src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts:379-410`. It is exactly 600 lines, so this must be extracted to the specified new `src/execution/story-orchestrator/nbf-seed.ts`, not extended inline. The new seam must select only configured review sources, ignore a missing selected phase, use `actionableAdvisoryFindings` unchanged (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:65-74`), deduplicate overlapping findings, and preserve green/rectification/story-id/`shouldRunNonBlockingFix` gates. All review phases are excluded from NBF revalidation by `nonBlockingExcludePhases` (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:85-87`), and both phase names map to state slots in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:224-225`; no revalidation or implementer-source expansion is needed. `test/unit/execution/non-blocking-fix-wiring.test.ts` already stubs the NBF runner through the phase-completion path and is the integration seam.

For static rules, the provider computes a budget result then emits approaching and truncation warnings without checking `this.enforceBudget` at `src/context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts:371-390`; only afterward does it choose retained versus all sections, and notice chunks remain enforcement-only (`src/context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts:391-460`). This source file is 597/600 lines, so use a net-neutral or shrinking conditional wording change. Do not alter returned chunks, notices, or `buildSectionBudgetPressure` output. `ProviderBudgetPressure` incorrectly says dropped counts are zero unless enforced at `src/context/engine/manifest-types.ts:31-38`; change the two field comments to describe would-be discards in soft mode and `overageTokens` as the enforcement-independent signal. Existing provider tests are in `test/unit/context/engine/providers/static-rules.test.ts` and related static-rules files; `test/unit/log-format/run-summary.test.ts:88` anchors the old enforced truncation message, which must remain unchanged.

Risks are schema-default type fallout, silent legacy-key stripping, wrong layer precedence, retaining an adversarial-only assembly guard, unstable duplicate identity, and accidentally changing static-rules output while correcting its logs. The migration must run per raw layer before merge; NBF must remain opt-in with the adversarial-only default; and soft mode must still deliver all sections while retaining pressure counts for would-be drops.
outOfScope: Per-reviewer `blockingThreshold` configuration (`review.semantic.blockingThreshold` / `review.adversarial.blockingThreshold`). One shared threshold stays the only threshold; if per-reviewer thresholds are wanted they are a separate change, landing after this one so the union's semantics are already pinned by tests.

Changing what `budgetPressure.droppedCount` counts in soft mode. It remains a pressure signal — the count of sections that would be dropped — and the existing US-003 AC 3 assertion at `static-rules.test.ts:667` stays green. Only the log wording and the field documentation change.
Changing nbf's `scope`, `sourceDiffCap`, `regressionAttempts` or `verifierGuard` semantics, or making any of them per-source. One fix pass, one set of knobs.

Adding a category filter to what nbf seeds. `actionableAdvisoryFindings` filters on `actionRequired`, `acDropped` and recurrence-retirement only, never on `category`, so an adversarial `out-of-scope` finding is seeded today and still will be. Whether a scope violation should drive an automated fix is #1359's decision to make, and this change must not settle it through a side door — the same reason `acDropped` findings are filtered at the seeding site rather than at the reviewer (`non-blocking-fix.ts:66-71`, holding #1801). The union adds nothing here either way: `out-of-scope` is an adversarial-only category, and adversarial was already the seeded source.
Adding a `category` to semantic-review findings. 132 of 145 carry none today; that is a reviewer-prompt question, not a seeding question.
Emitting a `stale` chunk-exclusion reason, persisting `ChunkKind`, or any curator heuristic change (#1931, #1930, #1445).
Aggregating the plan-time Context Files drop telemetry (#1474).
